intro: Some landmark decoders choose the strongest discrete location rather than averaging confidence across the image. Resolve ties consistently.
task: Return the row-column coordinates and value of the first maximum in each heatmap.
requirements: heatmaps has shape batch-by-height-by-width and may contain negative values.
Return {"coordinates": batch-by-2 integer matrix, "score": vector}. Break ties by the smallest row, then the smallest column (row-major order).

Use finite real numeric values of magnitude at most 1e6, excluding boolean inputs. Each array axis has 1..64 entries and at most 65536 elements total unless a stricter bound is stated. Return NumPy arrays for array outputs, preserve caller inputs, and raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

examples.name: Rectangular map
examples.output:
{'coordinates': [[1, 0]], 'score': [6.0]}
(NumPy arrays shown as lists; rounded to 12 significant digits.)

examples.name: Tied maxima
examples.output:
{'coordinates': [[0, 1]], 'score': [3.0]}
(NumPy arrays shown as lists; rounded to 12 significant digits.)

examples.name: All negative
examples.output:
{'coordinates': [[0, 1]], 'score': [-2.0]}
(NumPy arrays shown as lists; rounded to 12 significant digits.)

hints.title: Follow the data
hints.body: Find the flat index of each maximum, then use division and remainder by image width.

hints.title: Check the boundary
hints.body: Using height in the index conversion fails for rectangular maps.

explanation: Peak decoding selects a location that actually attains the largest supplied score. It can differ substantially from the center of mass when the map contains multiple modes.
Deterministic row-major tie handling makes equal-score results reproducible. The returned score need not be a probability because this contract accepts any finite response values.
